notes: Pre-pulse expands droplet; main pulse creates hot plasma

notes: EUV cannot pass through ordinary glass/air

notes: Required because EUV is absorbed by air

name: High-NA faster reticle stage
notes: Required to maintain productivity with smaller exposure field

name: Vessel metrology sensors
notes: ASML describes lasers, cameras and sensors used to regulate stable plasma and target timing

name: Laser-droplet synchronization system
notes: Synchronization is required to hit moving tin droplets at production rate

name: Tin capture and removal system
notes: ASML identifies tin contamination as a source problem and describes capture/removal research

name: Magnetic-field debris mitigation
notes: Published HVM source work describes debris mitigation by magnetic field

name: Multilayer Bragg mirror coating
notes: ASML states each EUV mirror has more than 100 engineered layers

name: Ultra-smooth EUV mirror
notes: ASML describes mirror smoothness requirement at approximately less than one atom thickness

name: Active mirror positioning/actuation
notes: ASML describes thousands of actuators for precise optical-element adjustment

name: Thermal-distortion compensation
notes: Repeated EUV pulses heat optics; active compensation is used to control distortion

name: High-precision multilayer collector
notes: Meaningful engineering alternative within the same mirror-based physics; no unsupported performance claim

name: Flattened tin droplet before main pulse
notes: ASML reports flattening the tin droplet before the explosion increased EUV light output

name: Dual-pulse CO2 architecture
